title: The first Buddha
translation: When I was eight, I asked my father, "What is a Buddha?"
"A Buddha is what a person becomes," he said.
"How does a person become a Buddha?"
"By following the teaching of a Buddha."
"Then who taught the Buddha who taught him?"
"He became one by following the teaching of the Buddha before him."
"Then the very first Buddha, the one who started the teaching. What kind of Buddha was he?"
"Oh, he fell from the sky, I suppose," my father said. "Or came up out of the ground." And he laughed.
"He backed me into a corner, and I couldn't answer," he told everyone, and he had great fun with it.
original: {八|や}つになりし{年|とし}、{父|ちち}に{問|と}ひていはく、「{仏|ほとけ}はいかなるものにか{候|さうらふ}らむ。」といふ。
{父|ちち}がいはく、「{仏|ほとけ}には{人|ひと}のなりたるなり。」と。
また{問|と}ふ、「{人|ひと}は{何|なに}として{仏|ほとけ}にはなり{候|さうらふ}やらむ。」と、{父|ちち}また、「{仏|ほとけ}のをしへによりてなるなり。」とこたふ。
また{問|と}ふ、「{教|をし}へ{候|さうら}ひける{仏|ほとけ}をば、{何|なに}がをしへ{候|さうら}ひける。」と。
また{答|こた}ふ、「それもまた、さきの{仏|ほとけ}のをしへによりてなり{給|たま}ふなり。」と。
{又|また}{問|と}ふ、「その{教|をし}へはじめ{候|さうら}ひける{第一|だいいち}の{仏|ほとけ}は、いかなる{仏|ほとけ}にか{候|さうら}ひける。」といふとき、{父|ちち}、「{空|そら}よりや{降|ふ}りけむ、{土|つち}よりやわきけむ。」といひて{笑|わら}ふ。
「{問|と}ひつめられてえ{答|こた}へずなり{侍|はべ}りつ。」と{諸人|しよにん}にかたりて{興|きよう}じき。
literal: In the year I turned eight, I asked my father, saying, 'What kind of thing might a Buddha be?'
My father said, 'A Buddha is what a person has become.'
Again I asked, 'How does a person become a Buddha?', and my father again answered, 'He becomes one through the teaching of a Buddha.'
Again I asked, 'The Buddha who taught: what taught him?'
Again he answered, 'He too became one through the teaching of an earlier Buddha.'
Again I asked, 'The first Buddha, who began the teaching: what kind of Buddha was he?', and then my father said, 'Perhaps he fell from the sky, perhaps he sprang from the earth', and laughed.
'I was pressed with questions and could not answer,' he told many people, and was amused.

notes.text: The last section of the book. The 1925 edition identifies the father as Urabe no Kaneaki, a junior assistant minister in the Ministry of Ceremonial (治部少輔). The Urabe were a family of diviners and Shinto priests at court. The book closes after two stern sections on Buddhist practice (241 and 242) on a memory of childhood.

notes.quote: いかなるものにか候らむ
notes.text: The boy speaks to his father in polite {候|さうらふ} style all the way through. The translation keeps his questions plain.

notes.quote: 仏には人のなりたるなり
notes.text: 'A Buddha is what a person has become.' This is the standard answer: a Buddha is someone who has become enlightened, not a god who was always there.
{何|なに}: literally 'what', but in this period it can also ask about a person. The translation uses 'who'.

notes.quote: 空よりや降りけむ、土よりやわきけむ
notes.text: や … けむ: a guess about the past, 'did he perhaps…?'. The father has no answer and makes a joke of it.

notes.quote: 問ひつめられてえ答へずなり侍りつ
notes.text: え … ず: 'could not'. 問ひつむ: 'to press with questions, to corner' (modern {問|と}い{詰|つ}める). The father tells the story against himself, politely ({侍|はべ}り), to his listeners.
{興|きよう}ず: 'to be amused, to enjoy'. き: the past of what the writer saw himself. These are the last words of Tsurezuregusa.
